page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance trade-off between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core performance is relatively low, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the bottom 25%, while single-threaded gzip compression falls into the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core performance is consistently average, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all positioning in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with Passmark memory and database operations, also align with average tier performance.

Given the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-core processing capabilities, this instance is suited for workloads that scale horizontally across multiple cores rather than those requiring high single-thread performance. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, Redis database operations, software compilation, and moderate LLM inference tasks using small to medium models. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile offers a standard resource density for general-purpose enterprise applications that do not require local SSD storage or GPU acceleration.
